newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Know-how exists to slash EU air pollution - WWF.
newsitem.headline: Know-how exists to slash EU air pollution - WWF.

text.p: Energy use reductions exploiting existing technologies and other proven measures could help EU countries cut carbon dioxide emissions in line with some of the tightest targets, a World Wide Fund for Nature report says.
The report released on Thursday said the most significant carbon dioxide (CO2) cuts could come in the residential sector followed by heavy industry, transport and the service sector.
"By starting in 1998 with a range of proven policies and measures, the EU could cut these emissions to 14 percent below 1990 levels by 2005," the report said.

Small island states, threatened by the rising sea levels which have been predicted as a result of increased global temperatures, have called on industrial countries such as the EU's 15 countries, the United States, Canada and Japan to slash their CO2 emissions by 2005.

"The EU has a depressing record of missed opportunites on climate change and no clear idea of how it is going to tackle this problem in the future," WWF climate campaigner Andrew Kerr told a news conference.

"Without ministerial backing for an EU climate protection strategy and firm emission targets the EU will be unable to combat the causes of climate change at home. And it will lose its ability to exert leverage on the international negotiations," Kerr said.

European Union environment ministers are due at a regular meeting next month to discuss climate policy days ahead of a full-scale meeting of the countries involved in United Nations climate change negotiations.

U.N. climate scientists have said human actions have a discernable influence on climate change with increased emissions of various gases such as CO2 trapping solar energy in the atmosphere and warming the air in a greenhouse effect.
